headline: Benchmarks expose robustness and reproducibility gaps in biological machine learning…
label: Benchmarking Foundation Models Biology
summary: Recent benchmarks and audits test whether foundation models and ML pipelines in omics hold up under distribution shift and reproducibility checks.
synthesis: The common thread is stress-testing learned models in computational biology under realistic conditions. Single-cell foundation models are assessed on multiple axes: VCBench finds linear baselines match or beat most models on five testable dimensions, and a systematic benchmark of 20 models across 6 tasks and 1,607 datasets examines zero-shot utility and robustness to structural perturbations. Tabular foundation models face query distribution shifts in six gut microbiome datasets, with zero-imputation identified as most harmful. Reproducibility is audited directly: only 17 of 50 protein-ligand binding affinity models were runnable and 9 statistically reproducible on CASF-2016, and a microbial network benchmark finds synthetic SPIEC-EASI data diverges from real data. What is new is the shift from reporting accuracy on curated splits toward perturbation testing, leakage-free validation, and reproducibility checklists. KG-TRACE adds a grounding metric for AMR prediction, and DSEN separates shared from lineage-specific drug-response blocks under leakage-free cross-validation across 265 drugs.
